messages:
Allison Grant: seeing repeated export job timeouts in the internal load test run (staging). not a full incident yet but feels incident-adjacent. anyone else watching? p95 export duration spiking and a bunch of jobs dying at ~60s.

Incident Bot: :warning: Alert (staging): `usage-insights-export-job-timeout-rate` > 5% for 10m. Current: 18.7%. Runbook: https://go.redwood/runbooks/usage-insights/export-timeouts

Logan Wright: yep, we kicked off the load test around 09:40. timeout rate correlates exactly. i can pause the test if needed.

Allison Grant: pls don’t pause yet—let’s capture enough data to be confident, then we’ll dial it back. which timeout is it? worker side or API gateway?

Mei Lin: looking now. export-worker logs show `context deadline exceeded` when pulling aggregates + formatting CSV. API is returning 504 from the download endpoint when the job hasn’t completed.

Chloe Martin: FYI current flow is: create export job -> poll -> download. the polling endpoint is fine. the download endpoint triggers “finalize file if not ready” (legacy behavior) and can block.

Jada Williams: ^ that “finalize on download” is probably the culprit. we intended it as a convenience but under load it’s a footgun.

Kevin Osei: security angle: we also have audit events firing twice in some cases (create + download triggers finalize). not ideal but not the main issue.

Allison Grant: do we have a dashboard link w/ the export worker saturation + queue depth?

Mei Lin: Grafana staging: https://grafana.redwood/staging/d/usage-insights-export
- queue depth went from ~20 to 480 in ~12m
- worker CPU pegged, memory hitting limit (OOM-kills 2 pods)
- avg job size jumped (requests asking for 30d range)

Thomas Baird: what are the export guardrails currently? max rows / max time range?

Chloe Martin: currently max time range = 31d, max rows “soft” (we stop at 250k records) but it’s after query + join. CSV formatting happens in-memory.

Allison Grant: ok so we’re spending resources before we discover we’re over budget. can we fail fast based on estimated cardinality (routes * models * hours)?

Mei Lin: we can approximate. request has filters (org/project/env/region/route). for the load test we used only org/project, so worst-case.

Logan Wright: load test config was 200 concurrent export requests, 50% set to 30d, no route filter. i can reduce concurrency, but we should still hotfix.

Felix Schneider: console currently offers “Last 30 days” as a default option in staging (feature flag on). could be why folks keep picking it.

Allison Grant: mitigation plan options:
1) immediate: reduce default time range in UI + enforce smaller max in API
2) hotfix: make download endpoint never finalize (must be READY)
3) medium: stream CSV / chunked writes to S3
Which can we do today?

Jada Williams: (2) is small + safest. make `GET /exports/{id}/download` return 409 if state != READY, with retry-after. the console already polls.

Chloe Martin: +1. will require small console tweak to handle 409 gracefully (but it already retries on 404/409 from older behavior). still, i’ll confirm.

Mei Lin: (1) also quick: change max range to 7d for now, and force route/model breakdown pagination in export. but that’s a product call.

Logan Wright: PM (Paula) is in meetings but i can ping. if we cap at 7d temporarily just for beta/staging, that’s probably ok.

Kevin Osei: if we change download semantics, make sure audit log still records download attempts even if not ready (we want evidence). but don’t double-count successful downloads.

Allison Grant: for now, prioritize service health + no customer impact. staging only but we’re close to beta. let’s do (2) + tighter server-side limits, then re-run load.

Thomas Baird: also: route cardinality. if they request “all routes”, it’s going to explode. can we require at least one of: route prefix filter OR limit top N routes for export?

Jada Williams: we can set `max_routes=500` for export job generation and include a note in metadata “truncated”. not perfect but avoids death.

Mei Lin: quick reality check: timeout is 60s because worker has hard deadline for the “format+upload” step. we can bump to 180s but then we just move the cliff.

Allison Grant: agreed—don’t just raise timeouts as a fix. also OOMs suggest we need streaming writes.

Chloe Martin: immediate patch proposal:
- worker writes CSV to temp file stream (node stream -> gzip -> upload) instead of building whole string
- download endpoint: no finalize; only serves READY
This is more than “tiny” though.

Jada Williams: we can split:
Hotfix A (today): download endpoint 409 if not READY + enforce max range 7d for staging/beta flag
Hotfix B (this week): stream CSV generation + reduce memory

Allison Grant: sounds right. can we also add a circuit breaker: if queue depth > X, reject new export job creations with 429 + message “try later”?

Mei Lin: yes. export-service can check Redis queue depth. if > 300, return 429 with `Retry-After: 60`.

Logan Wright: i’ll own the “pause load test” once Hotfix A is in staging so we can validate. until then i’ll lower concurrency to 50 and remove 30d requests.

Allison Grant: ok. who’s doing what?
- Chloe/Jada: API change for download semantics + status code contract
- Mei: queue depth guardrail + staging max range cap
- Kevin: audit log behavior check
I’ll update the oncall notes + watch dashboards.

Kevin Osei: ack. re audit events: currently we emit:
`usage_export.created`
`usage_export.downloaded`
If we return 409, we should NOT emit `downloaded`. we can emit `usage_export.download_attempted` if we want, but that’s a schema change. suggest no new event in hotfix.

Allison Grant: +1 no schema changes in hotfix. keep it simple.

Chloe Martin: pushing a quick PR to redwood service now. will ping when staging deploy is ready. change is basically:
- if export.state != READY -> return 409
- remove code path that calls finalize()

Jada Williams: i’ll review. also we should ensure console handles 409 as “still processing” not “hard error”. Felix can sanity check UI.

Felix Schneider: i can test on staging once deployed. console currently polls `/exports/{id}` until READY, so download shouldn’t even happen early, but we have a race when user clicks twice.

Mei Lin: adding cap to export job request: `max_window_days=7` for `beta_usage_insights_exports` flag on. if request > 7d -> 400 with message. ok?

Allison Grant: do 400 with actionable message (pick shorter range). for 429 queue depth, include retry-after.

Thomas Baird: please also add metrics:
- rejected_export_jobs_total{reason=queue_depth|max_window}
- download_not_ready_total
This will help us tune.

Mei Lin: yup.

Logan Wright: pinged Paula in #product. also i’ll update load test harness to include a route filter by default. we were unrealistic.

Allison Grant: unrealistic but useful—this is exactly what customers will do when Finance asks for “everything”.

Incident Bot: Update: Alert (staging) `usage-insights-export-job-timeout-rate` still firing. Current: 22.1%.

Chloe Martin: PR up: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/15485 (part of it). includes only the 409-on-download + remove finalize-on-download. requesting quick review from Jada + Allison.

Jada Williams: reviewing now. comment: make sure 409 body is stable JSON `{code, message}` consistent w API standards.

Chloe Martin: fixed. returning `{"code":"EXPORT_NOT_READY","message":"Export is still processing. Please retry after it reaches READY."}` and `Retry-After: 5`.

Allison Grant: reviewed. looks good. ship to staging behind `export_download_requires_ready` flag?

Chloe Martin: added flag default ON in staging, OFF elsewhere. we can flip gradually.

Mei Lin: queue depth reject + max window cap PR is separate: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/15506 (staging only). adds metrics too.

Kevin Osei: skimmed audit path. with the new behavior, we only emit `usage_export.downloaded` when state=READY and file served. good.

Felix Schneider: can confirm console already waits for READY before enabling Download button. 409 should only happen if someone hits the endpoint directly or there’s a race. so safe.

Allison Grant: ok let’s deploy both PRs to staging. once live, Logan re-run higher concurrency and we’ll see if timeouts drop.

Logan Wright: will do. i’ll start with 100 concurrent create jobs but limit to 7d. then we can test queue depth behavior separately.

Incident Bot: :white_check_mark: Alert recovered (staging): `usage-insights-export-job-timeout-rate` back to 3.2% for 10m.

Allison Grant: nice. still want to address OOMs though. Mei, are workers still getting killed?

Mei Lin: OOMs stopped once queue stabilized. but we’re still memory heavy on the biggest exports. streaming CSV is still needed for GA.

Allison Grant: agreed. let’s track as follow-up and add a rollback trigger for beta: if timeout rate > 5% or queue depth > 300 sustained, disable exports flag.

Thomas Baird: i’ll add an alert suggestion in the SRE checklist: `export_queue_depth` + `export_worker_oom_kills`.

Allison Grant: thanks. also please drop a note in #eng-platform thread w/ the new 409 contract so nobody is surprised.

Chloe Martin: will do.

Logan Wright: load test results post-hotfix: 100 concurrent exports, 7d window:
- success 99.4%
- p95 job duration 18s
- download 409s: 12 (expected due to direct download hammer in harness)
Looks good.

Allison Grant: perfect. marking this as incident-adjacent resolved for staging. next: streaming generation + revisit product defaults for 30d exports before beta expands.
